dmn.name: Anhalonium lewinii
dmn.feeling: Loss of ego-boundary; merges with surroundings; dissociates from a felt void in identity.
dmn.why: The pathology is a disturbance of self-referential processing itself — depersonalisation and boundary-loss are Default-Mode phenomena turned pathological, not fear or somatic arousal.

dmn.name: Antimonium crudum
dmn.feeling: World is disappointing, so he withdraws and idealises — lives inside nostalgic, sentimental fantasy rather than facing reality.
dmn.why: Sustained internal idealisation/fantasy that substitutes for engagement with the present is a rumination-adjacent loop — attention is captured by an internally generated narrative.

dmn.name: Cannabis indica
dmn.feeling: Isolated in a "glass house"; builds elaborate fantasies and exaggerated inner perceptions rather than stepping into the outer world.
dmn.why: Classic internally-generated, self-referential narrative that displaces external engagement — the mind is "sticky" on its own content.

dmn.name: China officinalis
dmn.feeling: Feels persecuted and held back, so compensates by fantasising and theorising achievements — "builds castles in the air."
dmn.why: Chronic compensatory fantasy/theorising is a fixed internal loop standing in for real-world action, matching DMN's inward pull.

dmn.name: Coffea cruda
dmn.feeling: Mind racing with ideas and plans, cannot stop being mentally/physically active, marked insomnia from overactive thought.
dmn.why: Hyperactive, un-shutoffable ideation plus classic initial insomnia from mental overactivity is a near-literal match to the DM symptom profile.

dmn.name: Kalium phosphoricum
dmn.feeling: Mind full of thought and activity when unsupported; insomnia; eventually mental exhaustion ("impotency of his mind").
dmn.why: Insomnia driven by racing, anxious thought that cannot disengage — the DM "switch" failing to turn off at night.

dmn.name: Medorrhinum
dmn.feeling: Absorbed in his own thoughts, loses the thread of conversation, time distorts, familiar things feel unfamiliar.
dmn.why: Absent-mindedness and losing track of the external conversation because internal processing dominates is a direct DM marker ("internal distractibility").

dmn.name: Naja tripudians
dmn.feeling: Brooding, suicidal preoccupation with having done everything wrong; a split mind caught replaying the conflict.
dmn.why: Brooding on irreversible past wrongs that cannot be resolved is repetitive negative thinking focused on regret — DM's core loop.

dmn.name: Natrium carbonicum
dmn.feeling: Ennui and apprehension from being alone; blames self endlessly ("does everything wrong"); estranged, silently grieving.
dmn.why: Melancholic dwelling and self-blame that cannot be put down is the DM "broken record" of regret.

dmn.name: Natrium muriaticum
dmn.feeling: Dwells on past disagreeable occurrences, cannot forget; an idea "clings" and prevents sleep; silent grief, revengeful replaying.
dmn.why: The single clearest Default-Mode match in the Materia Medica — Sankaran's own description ("an idea clings, prevents sleep") is almost a paraphrase of the biotype's initial-insomnia-from-rumination marker.

sal.name: Aconitum napellus
sal.feeling: Sudden, intense panic from outside threat — racing pulse, palpitation, restlessness, cannot sit still.
sal.why: The textbook acute somatic panic attack: sudden autonomic storm, startle, restlessness — Salience's hyperactive alarm in its purest acute form.

sal.name: Argentum nitricum
sal.feeling: Anticipatory, phobic anxiety before performance or in closed/high places; fear of losing self-control; claustrophobia.
sal.why: Situational, autonomic, avoidance-driven anxiety (claustrophobia, stage fright, hurried restlessness) is the phobic face of an over-active salience alarm.

sal.name: Arsenicum album
sal.feeling: Hypochondriacal anxiety about health and security; restless, fastidious, cannot settle until everything is in order.
sal.why: Explicitly named in the Brain Circuits text itself as the somatic/hypochondriacal presentation of Salience dysfunction.

sal.name: Belladonna
sal.feeling: Sudden violent threat, must escape; throbbing carotids, palpitation, intense acute arousal that vanishes as fast as it came.
sal.why: Paroxysmal, purely somatic panic-and-escape reaction — alarm system firing and resetting abruptly.

sal.name: Calcarea arsenicosa
sal.feeling: Insecure and mistrustful; severe palpitation triggered by the least emotional upset.
sal.why: Palpitation from minimal emotional trigger is a direct autonomic/somatic marker of an over-sensitised alarm circuit.

sal.name: Calcarea carbonica
sal.feeling: Needs stability/protection; overwhelmed and retreating from cruelty, horror, or anything sensorily/emotionally intense.
sal.why: Avoidance is driven by being overwhelmed by external stimuli (violence on TV, loud events) rather than by low mood — a Salience-type overwhelm/avoidance pattern.

sal.name: Calcarea silicata
sal.feeling: Anticipatory anxiety before exams/interviews; uses health-anxiety to avoid performance demands.
sal.why: Anticipatory somatic anxiety used defensively to avoid exposure is characteristic Salience-circuit avoidance.

sal.name: Coca
sal.feeling: Feels it is too risky to leave the safety of his "castle"; isolates to avoid external threat while under pressure to perform.
sal.why: Avoidance driven by perceived external danger/risk, with somatic stage-fright, situates this in the threat-detection/avoidance axis of Salience.

sal.name: Cocculus indicus
sal.feeling: Nerves become "raw"; marked oversensitivity to noise, motion, odours; dulled, giddy, wants to lie still with eyes closed.
sal.why: Sensory-flooding and hypersensitivity to ordinary stimuli is close to a textbook description of Salience's broken sensory "filter."

sal.name: Cuprum metallicum
sal.feeling: Feels attacked, must defend; reactions come in sudden paroxysmal spasms/convulsions rather than continuously.
sal.why: Paroxysmal, all-or-nothing threat-response wired for sudden defensive mobilisation matches the alarm-circuit's episodic hyperactivation.

sal.name: Gelsemium sempervirens
sal.feeling: Ailments from anticipation/shock/bad news; loses control and balance; can freeze into a paralytic, immobile state.
sal.why: Anticipatory dread that culminates in a "frozen" collapse is exactly the overwhelmed/frozen reaction the Brain Circuits text uses to distinguish Salience from Negative Affect.

sal.name: Kalium arsenicosum
sal.feeling: Anxious to the point of feeling "crazy"; extremely edgy, startles at the slightest noise.
sal.why: Marked startle and edge-of-the-seat autonomic arousal is a direct Salience marker.

sal.name: Kalium carbonicum
sal.feeling: Fear of being alone; startles easily from noise or touch; frightened at trifles.
sal.why: Trigger-happy startle response to minor stimuli is the hallmark hyperactive alarm of Salience dysfunction.

sal.name: Lycopodium clavatum
sal.feeling: Fear of undertaking anything new or challenging, though ambitious and capable once started.
sal.why: Anticipatory avoidance of situations (not lack of desire) places this alongside Argentum nitricum on the phobic-avoidance end of Salience.

sal.name: Phosphorus
sal.feeling: Wide-ranging emotional/sensory reactivity; vulnerable to environmental and emotional stimuli; "hot flushes from excitement," fear of thunderstorms.
sal.why: Heightened autonomic and sensory reactivity to external stimuli (thunderstorms, excitement) reflects an easily-triggered salience/interoceptive system, even though the coping style is approach rather than avoidance.

sal.name: Rhus toxicodendron
sal.feeling: Constant anxiety "as if something is going to happen"; restless, cannot rest in any position; hypervigilant at night.
sal.why: Persistent unlocalised somatic restlessness and hypervigilance without a clear external trigger is classic Salience-circuit background arousal.

sal.name: Stramonium
sal.feeling: Acute terror of being abandoned in the dark; clings to whatever is near; familiar things suddenly feel strange.
sal.why: Acute panic with disorientation and clinging for safety is the somatic-overwhelm presentation of an over-firing alarm circuit.

sal.name: Strontium carbonicum
sal.feeling: Anxious about new/unknown tasks; needs an experienced guide to venture out safely.
sal.why: Situational anticipatory anxiety resolved only by external reassurance mirrors Salience's avoidance-until-safety-confirmed pattern.

sal.name: Theridion curassavicum
sal.feeling: Marked aggravation and startle from noise; fear of being trapped or killed if without a partner.
sal.why: Noise-triggered startle and sensory intolerance is a direct Salience marker.

sal.name: Zincum metallicum
sal.feeling: Constant anxiety of being pursued/arrested; twitching, restless legs, a state of continuous "ready alertness."
sal.why: Continuous (not paroxysmal) hyperarousal and motor restlessness is the sustained-alarm variant of Salience dysfunction.

neg.name: Ambra grisea
neg.feeling: Intense shame — feels intrinsically "disgusting"; catastrophic embarrassment if exposed.
neg.why: Catastrophic anticipation of humiliation and rejection if one's flaw is seen is rejection-sensitivity in its most acute form.

neg.name: Aurum metallicum
neg.feeling: Crushing guilt and despair when impossible self-imposed duties are not met; suicidal when confidence of others is lost.
neg.why: Guilt, misery and mood-congruent despair triggered by (perceived) failure and disapproval is the Negative Affect biotype's dysphoria.

neg.name: Bryonia alba
neg.feeling: Driven by fear of poverty/loss; dry, business-focused, irritable if disturbed from the effort to avert loss.
neg.why: The organising fear is of catastrophic material loss — a threat-avoidance drive coloured by irritability rather than somatic panic.

neg.name: Calcarea bromata
neg.feeling: Fear of being falsely accused or pounced upon by the very person he depends on for security.
neg.why: Catastrophic anticipation of blame/punishment from a trusted figure is classic threat-perception with rejection overtones.

neg.name: Calcarea fluorica
neg.feeling: Chronic fear that hard-won security is eroding and will collapse into poverty or ruin.
neg.why: Persistent catastrophic fear about an unstable future is mood-congruent negative-bias thinking about threat.

neg.name: Calcarea iodata
neg.feeling: Fear of being betrayed or starved by the one depended on, masked by forced cheerfulness.
neg.why: Fear of betrayal with an underlying catastrophic expectation of harm is core Negative Affect, with the cheerful surface as compensation.

neg.name: Calcarea phosphorica
neg.feeling: Feels unloved at home, seeks affection elsewhere, restless travel to find connection.
neg.why: The driving feeling is of being insufficiently loved — an attachment-threat / rejection theme, not anhedonia (the person actively seeks connection).

neg.name: Calcarea sulphurica
neg.feeling: Feels perpetually unappreciated and passed over; laments, jealous of others' recognition.
neg.why: Chronic sense of being undervalued/rejected by the people one depends on is rejection sensitivity.

neg.name: Cantharis vesicatoria
neg.feeling: Violent rage when offended; terror of being throttled by cold hands in the dark.
neg.why: Fear and rage responses to perceived threat/injury, with catastrophic imagery, sit in the fear/anger cluster of Negative Affect.

neg.name: Causticum
neg.feeling: Anxious for the safety of family/group; fears something bad will happen to them.
neg.why: Chronic catastrophic anticipation on behalf of loved ones is threat-focused, mood-congruent worry.

neg.name: Chocolate
neg.feeling: Forsaken by early separation from mother; craves warmth, fears being injured, feels estranged from her world.
neg.why: Attachment rupture with lasting forsaken/estranged feeling is a rejection/abandonment-driven Negative Affect picture.

neg.name: Cicuta virosa
neg.feeling: Deeply hurt in the past, regressed and fearful; hateful, suspicious and contemptuous of men.
neg.why: Trauma history producing lasting mistrust and hostility is exactly the early-life-trauma-sensitised amygdala picture the Brain Circuits text describes.

neg.name: Cyclamen europaeum
neg.feeling: Guilt-ridden, feels like a criminal for an unspoken "wrong," isolates in silent self-blame.
neg.why: Sustained guilt and self-blame with mood-congruent misery is core Negative Affect.

neg.name: Drosera rotundifolia
neg.feeling: Feels persecuted, deceived and stabbed in the back by friends; suspicious, prone to violent outbursts.
neg.why: Catastrophizing about being betrayed by trusted people, with hostile/suspicious bias, matches Negative Affect's negative interpretive bias.

neg.name: Elaps corallinus
neg.feeling: Fear of crashing down from a high social position; anxious for the safety and image of loved ones.
neg.why: Catastrophic fear of loss of standing/safety, chronically anticipated, is threat-biased cognition.

neg.name: Hepar sulphur
neg.feeling: Feels terribly offended and humiliated by those meant to protect him; explosively violent when provoked.
neg.why: Misery and rage triggered by perceived humiliation from a trusted figure is Negative Affect's threat/rejection axis, at high intensity.

neg.name: Hippomanes
neg.feeling: Suppressed aggression and sexuality collapse into suicidal despondency, sitting apart from the world.
neg.why: Despondent misery following suppression/inability to express instinct is dysphoric, mood-congruent despair.

neg.name: Hura brasiliensis
neg.feeling: Feels castaway, despised, unlucky — like a leper whose friends have all deserted him.
neg.why: Hopeless, forsaken misery with catastrophic and mood-congruent narrative ("once ruined, always ruined") is textbook Negative Affect.

neg.name: Hyoscyamus niger
neg.feeling: Sudden terror of being betrayed and deserted by the one depended on; jealous, suspicious, occasionally violent.
neg.why: Acute fear of abandonment/betrayal with jealousy and suspicion is a Negative Affect presentation, even though its onset is acute.

neg.name: Kalium iodatum
neg.feeling: Fear of being betrayed or stabbed in the back by family, masked by forced wit and cheer.
neg.why: Underlying catastrophic fear of betrayal from the people one is most attached to.

neg.name: Kalium sulphuricum
neg.feeling: Feels disgraced and insulted by the group whose esteem he seeks; discouraged, easily hurt.
neg.why: Chronic rejection sensitivity and disgrace-anticipation.

neg.name: Lac caninum
neg.feeling: Low self-worth from constant unfavourable comparison; feels "not good enough," despised.
neg.why: Persistent negative self-referential bias and rejection sensitivity from comparison is core Negative Affect.

neg.name: Lac vaccinum defloratum
neg.feeling: Fears rejection by the community; a tremendous sense of injustice; bears suffering silently.
neg.why: Anticipated social rejection with a strong injustice/threat narrative.

neg.name: Lachesis mutus
neg.feeling: Jealous rivalry, suspects conspiracies, must be "one-up" on a threatening competitor.
neg.why: Suspicious, threat-biased interpretation of relationships (rivals, conspiracies) is a Negative Affect cognitive pattern, with jealousy as the mood colour.

neg.name: Magnesium muriaticum
neg.feeling: Fears betrayal by friends; reserved, keeps emotional distance to avoid being let down.
neg.why: Anticipated betrayal of trust driving guardedness is rejection-sensitive threat-bias.

neg.name: Magnesium sulphuricum
neg.feeling: Anxiety about acceptance out of proportion to the situation; fears rejection if she does not appear "good enough."
neg.why: Disproportionate catastrophic fear of rejection is mood-congruent negative bias.

neg.name: Natrium sulphuricum
neg.feeling: Feels scorned and unappreciated; suicidal thoughts, guilt and remorse; "succeeds never."
neg.why: Misery, guilt and a catastrophizing self-narrative ("nothing ever works") is classic Negative Affect dysphoria.

neg.name: Nitricum acidum
neg.feeling: Constant sense of threat across health, work and relationships; hard, unforgiving, suspicious of enemies.
neg.why: Chronic threat-perception with hostile, mistrustful bias, and a fixed hard/enemy narrative, matches Negative Affect closely.

neg.name: Palladium metallicum
neg.feeling: Feels neglected and insulted if she does not earn others' good opinion.
neg.why: Rejection sensitivity tied directly to fear of others' disapproval.

neg.name: Paris quadrifolia
neg.feeling: The isolated, unattended child; feels inferior, seeks attention through foolish display.
neg.why: Chronic feeling of neglect/inferiority is a rejection-driven Negative Affect presentation.

neg.name: Platinum metallicum
neg.feeling: Feels humiliated and crushed, must grow "large" to survive; contemptuous of ordinary people while isolated.
neg.why: Humiliation-driven catastrophic self-narrative with contempt as a defensive mood colour.

neg.name: Plumbum metallicum
neg.feeling: Believes he is surrounded by murderers/conspirators; fears assassination.
neg.why: Extreme, fixed persecutory threat-bias is Negative Affect at its most severe.

neg.name: Pulsatilla pratensis
neg.feeling: Feels forsaken if not given tenderness; weeps, moods shift easily, dependent on comfort.
neg.why: The organising fear is of abandonment/rejection, soothed only by consolation — an attachment-threat presentation.

neg.name: Sulphur
neg.feeling: Feels scorned, put down, embarrassed; constant struggle to avoid humiliation and regain respect.
neg.why: Chronic anticipated scorn and embarrassment driving compensatory effort is rejection-sensitivity/threat-bias.

neg.name: Veratrum album
neg.feeling: Has lost social standing and must regain it urgently by any means, even fraud or show.
neg.why: Catastrophic fear of ruined status driving desperate, threat-avoidant compensation.

pos.name: Helleborus niger
pos.feeling: Profoundly insensitive to both pleasure and pain; completely shut off, dull, unregistering of the world.
pos.why: The single clearest anhedonic remedy in the book — indifference to pleasure and pain alike is the Positive Affect biotype's defining "blahs," taken to an extreme.

pos.name: Magnesium carbonicum
pos.feeling: Deep unmet dependency needs are repressed; becomes placid, flat, emotionally low-key and undemanding.
pos.why: Repression producing a flattened, low-emotional-expression baseline (rather than active distress) mirrors the reward-blunted, motivation-poor presentation of Positive Affect dysfunction.

pos.name: Phosphoricum acidum
pos.feeling: Exhausted from caring for others without reward; becomes dull, sluggish, indifferent, apathetic — "unequal struggle."
pos.why: The endpoint is explicit apathy and indifference after effort goes unrewarded — a burnt-out reward system, not active misery.

pos.name: Rheum palmatum
pos.feeling: The unattended child becomes indifferent to everything, asks for nothing, weeps without apparent cause.
pos.why: Indifference and lack of demand/initiative in the neglected state is a flattened-reward presentation (contrasted with the alternating demanding state, which is a separate, impulsive facet).

pos.name: Sepia officinalis
pos.feeling: Worn out from doing what she does not want to; becomes indifferent and averse even to husband and children — doesn't want treatment either.
pos.why: The well-known "failed" Sepia state is defined by indifference and aversion to the very relationships that should be rewarding — loss of reward signal from formerly valued things.

att.name: Baryta arsenicosa
att.feeling: Total incapacity and dependence; shy, nervous, easily panicked but fundamentally unable to function alone.
att.why: The core deficit is incapacity/inability to sustain independent function — closer to a cognitive-performance failure than an emotional one.

att.name: Baryta carbonica
att.feeling: Childish, totally dependent, irresolute; lacks imagination and creativity; needs everything explained and confirmed repeatedly.
att.why: Cognitive immaturity, poor imaginative/executive capacity, and reliance on others to think for him is a lethargic, under-recruited attentional/cognitive profile rather than active dyscontrol.

att.name: Baryta phosphorica
att.feeling: Combines Baryta's incapacity with Phosphorus's need for care; can drift between independence and dependent anxiety.
att.why: Same incapacity-driven cognitive profile as the other Baryta salts.

att.name: Baryta sulphurica
att.feeling: Weak memory, aversion to work, loss of will; struggles to mix or integrate in new settings.
att.why: Explicit weak memory and "loss of will" (weak initiation, not impulsivity) fits the lethargic, under-engaged Attention profile.

att.name: Graphites
att.feeling: Cannot concentrate, restless when required to think or plan; absent-minded, easily confused, scattered.
att.why: Direct concentration failure, absent-mindedness and inability to plan is the clearest Attention-circuit language in the book.

att.name: Picricum acidum
att.feeling: Intellectual capacity feels stretched beyond its limit; brain-fatigue, dullness, mental work becomes impossible.
att.why: Explicit cognitive/attentional collapse from overload — "mental work impossible" mirrors the Attention biotype's cognitive-slowing hallmark exactly.

att.name: Selenium metallicum
att.feeling: Premature senility, weak memory, poor concentration, dullness and sluggishness.
att.why: Weak memory and concentration difficulty as the leading physical/mental markers is a direct Attention-circuit match.

cog.name: Alumina
cog.feeling: Identity so suppressed he doesn't know what he wants; weak will, loses control of thought and movement, can act impulsively/violently.
cog.why: Explicit loss of executive/volitional control ("weak will," impulsive acts he does not intend) is a direct Cognitive-Control failure.

cog.name: Anacardium orientale
cog.feeling: "Two wills" constantly opposing each other — angel or devil; irresolute, impulsive, absent-minded.
cog.why: Literal inability to reconcile or inhibit opposing impulses is a textbook executive-inhibition failure.

cog.name: Argentum metallicum
cog.feeling: Collapses under performance pressure — loses his voice, his power, his mind; "prostration of mind," mental work becomes impossible.
cog.why: Executive/cognitive system failing specifically under demand, with alternating high-performance/total-collapse states, matches Cognitive Control's demand-sensitive breakdown.

cog.name: Bufo rana
cog.feeling: Cannot postpone any urge — must gratify immediately, whatever the impulse.
cog.why: Inability to delay gratification is the clearest possible description of a failed inhibitory "brake."

cog.name: Carcinosinum
cog.feeling: Drives himself toward near-impossible standards; tremendous need for control and order amid inner chaos.
cog.why: The central struggle is explicitly one of control — over self and surroundings — an executive-control theme, even though it usually succeeds rather than fails outright.

cog.name: Cina maritima
cog.feeling: Irritable tantrums, capricious demands, pushes away comfort even while wanting attention.
cog.why: Poor emotional self-regulation with reactive, uninhibited outbursts is a paediatric Cognitive-Control presentation.

cog.name: Crocus sativus
cog.feeling: Alternates suddenly between affectionate attractiveness and violent rage, followed by quick repentance.
cog.why: Rapid, uninhibited swings between opposite emotional/behavioural states, with immediate remorse, is a dyscontrol pattern.

cog.name: Ferrum metallicum
cog.feeling: Rigid, obstinate, "always in the right"; cannot yield or accept contradiction.
cog.why: Cognitive rigidity — inability to shift or accommodate — is the inflexibility facet of Cognitive Control dysfunction.

cog.name: Fluoricum acidum
cog.feeling: Impulsively forms and breaks relationships; disinhibited sexuality and activity; indifferent to consequences for family.
cog.why: Disinhibited, impulsive behaviour across relationships and impulse indicates a poorly regulated behavioural "brake."

cog.name: Lyssinum
cog.feeling: Violent rage toward the one he is dependent on, immediately followed by profound repentance.
cog.why: The rage-then-repentance cycle is a direct description of impulse breaking through inhibition, then control reasserting itself.

cog.name: Mercurius solubilis
cog.feeling: Sudden, impulsive violence when feeling dominated; extremes of precociousness and dullness; hasty, tumbling speech.
cog.why: Explosive impulsivity with poor inhibition of aggressive impulses is core Cognitive-Control dyscontrol.

cog.name: Nux vomica
cog.feeling: Impatient, hard-driving, gets things done "by hook or crook"; explosive anger; craves stimulants; cannot delay relief.
cog.why: Impulsivity, low frustration tolerance and craving/addictive tendencies ("insanity of drunkards") are classic disinhibition markers.

cog.name: Silicea terra
cog.feeling: Rigidly protects a fixed self-image; hard and inflexible, though inwardly yielding — "can break but not bend."
cog.why: Fixed, inflexible cognitive style organised entirely around maintaining control of one's image is the rigidity face of Cognitive Control.

cog.name: Staphisagria
cog.feeling: Suppresses anger to preserve dignity at all costs — until control finally breaks and trembling rage surfaces.
cog.why: The remedy's entire architecture is about inhibitory control of anger, and its failure when pushed too far — "I know I shouldn't, but I can't stop it" almost verbatim.

cog.name: Sulphuricum acidum
cog.feeling: Tremendous hurry in everything — eating, walking, working; cannot do things fast enough.
cog.why: Inability to regulate pace/urgency, with anxious drivenness that cannot be slowed voluntarily, is an inhibitory-control theme.

cog.name: Tarentula hispanica
cog.feeling: Impulsive, hysterical, flamboyant attention-seeking; hurried, mischievous, occasionally threatening.
cog.why: Impulsive, poorly-inhibited attention-seeking behaviour (including threatening displays) is a dyscontrol presentation.

cog.name: Thuja occidentalis
cog.feeling: Obsessive-compulsive fixed ideas and behaviour patterns; terror of exposing the "real," flawed self.
cog.why: Rigid, fixed-idea thinking that cannot be reasoned out of is the cognitive-rigidity face of Cognitive Control (Sankaran calls it explicitly a remedy "for neurosis, with obsessive-compulsive traits").

cog.name: Tuberculinum bovinum kent
cog.feeling: Cannot tolerate confinement or monotony; breaks out into rash, bold, sometimes destructive activity.
cog.why: Poor tolerance of restriction leading to impulsive, high-risk behaviour is a disinhibition pattern.

cog.name: Viola odorata
cog.feeling: Emotion is normally suppressed entirely by intellect — until an occasional upsurge of feeling takes the person over.
cog.why: A chronic inhibitory strategy that occasionally fails outright is a direct illustration of the brakes-failing mechanism Cognitive Control describes.
